request.title: CATACLYSM 0.7 — autonomous code-language council experiment
request.prompt: Resume the autonomous Cataclysm 0.7 content council at the Producer stage, using the verified Designer, Researcher, Engineer and Critic decisions from failed run 42311776452. Those agents already examined the private gameplay transcript and 12 visual frames and independently proposed concrete new mechanics; the Critic found all three compatible. Recover the actual prior decisions without replaying or exposing private recording data. The Producer independently chooses two or three of those vetted features, resolves any shared-symbol conflicts, sets interface contracts, and agrees a testable integration plan. The coding agent integrates ALL selected features together into one cohesive, playable mobile update. Add substantial game content, not mere numeric tuning or cosmetic changes. Preserve existing controls, Cataclysm identity, UI, score, boss fights, persistence, stable URL, and previous working mechanics. Release as Cataclysm 0.7 only after independent QA, touch emulation and verified production delivery.
acceptance: Designer, Researcher and Engineer independently propose three distinct, substantial content features with structured insert/modify/replace/remove operations and actual game-file symbols.

Critic evaluates compatibility, conflicts and tests for all three; Producer selects and records at least two compatible features with explicit integration order and shared code contracts before coding.
Each selected feature is actually implemented, playable, materially affects strategy or content, and is separately named and evidenced in the coder report and accepted receipt.

Existing Designer/Researcher/Engineer and Critic outputs are recovered from the verified previous video-backed council (run 42311776452), without repeating video inference or publishing transcript, frame images, or private agent input tasks.
Cataclysm retains existing movement/touch cancellation, auto-fire, scoring, boss flow, upgrades, pause/resume, restart, persistence, no external runtime services and stable play URL.
Independent mobile-touch Chromium checks pass at 360x780 and 390x844, verifying gameplay, pause, restart, HUD and browser errors; QA rejects missing selected gameplay.
The accepted game presents version 0.7 and a new run/build identifier; source is published only after hash-controlled acceptance and live-byte verification.

feature.name: Periodic Toxic Gas Clouds
feature.player_experience: Players must navigate away from temporary expanding gas clouds that emerge in different city locations during late nights. The clouds deal damage over time if the player remains inside, encouraging constant movement and map awareness. Visual and subtle audio warnings precede gas cloud formation, integrating tension spikes without breaking flow or UI simplicity. This mechanic ups late-game challenge and creates emergent gameplay moments leveraging existing controls.

code_changes.pseudo_code: // Modify to avoid spawning gas clouds too close to player or map edges

tests: Verify that toxic gas clouds spawn after night 8 at correct intervals and locations away from player and map edges
Verify gas clouds expand and shrink visually with correct timing and visual cues
Verify player receives damage over time if standing inside gas clouds
Verify notify messages and subtle warning sound play on gas cloud formation
Verify no changes to core player movement, input responsiveness, HUD, or upgrade menus
Validate no performance degradation on low-end mobile devices

feature.name: Pet Companion Upgrade
feature.player_experience: Players gain a new special upgrade option at milestone levels that, when upgraded, allows summoning a temporary AI-controlled pet cat. The companion autonomously targets and shoots at enemies with weaker projectiles for a limited duration, providing fire support. This adds a layer of tactical choice and increases survivability without changing control schemes or HUD layout.

code_changes.pseudo_code: // Define Pet companion entity properties; integrate into game state with limited lifetime and autonomous shooting behavior targeting nearest enemies independently at half player damage.
Add new special upgrade 'pet-companion' unlocked at milestones; limit total special upgrades as per existing rules; enable UI button for selection with description.
Update game tick to move pet companion independently, find closest enemy, and fire shot with lower damage; decrease pet active timer and remove when expired.
Implement logic so selecting 'pet-companion' adds pet entity with active timer; ensure upgrades obey existing upgrade caps and milestone constraints.
Render pet companion with visual style matching player's cat but smaller and distinct color, including a simple shooting animation.

tests: Start run, reach milestone level 3, verify 'pet-companion' upgrade option appears and is selectable.
Select 'pet-companion' upgrade, confirm pet companion spawns near player and autonomously fires at enemies.
Verify pet companion exists for limited duration and disappears afterward.
Confirm the pet companion projectiles deal damage but less than player's own shots.
Check that core controls (drag to move) remain unaffected with companion active.
Ensure upgrade menu disables irrelevant buttons properly and the new upgrade obeys special upgrade cap rules.

feature.name: Ghost Phaser Enemy
feature.player_experience: Players encounter occasional ghost-type enemies that move through walls and city blocks, forcing them to reposition strategically as these enemies periodically disable the player's automatic firing for short bursts, compelling avoidance and timing without changing controls or screen layout.

code_changes.pseudo_code: Add conditional to spawn 'ghost' variant starting at wave 6 with low spawn chance.

Add behavior for 'ghost' variant: moves ignoring obstacles; periodically triggers player's auto-fire disable buff for 2 seconds with cooldown; manage ghost phase timer and firing disable status on player.
Prevent shooting when player's 'autoFireDisabled' flag is set.
Render distinct translucent visual effect for ghost enemies and subtle icon or glow near player indicating auto-fire disabled status.

tests: Verify ghost enemies spawn starting night 6 and move through map obstacles without clipping.
Confirm player's automatic fire stops during ghost's disable effect and resumes after 2 seconds buff expires.
Check that ghost's disable effect does not stack or extend beyond cooldown period.
Ensure UI displays clear visual feedback when auto-fire is disabled.
Validate no changes in core input handling or mobile layout occur.
Verify no performance degradation on mobile viewport emulations.

assessments.mitigation: Implement priority layers for rendering and optimize update loops with throttling; add combined stress tests focusing on damage stacking and performance metrics under multiple active mechanics.
assessments.risk: Potential performance degradation and visual clutter on mobile devices; damage over time management overlapping with other mechanics might lead to stacking or obscure feedback.

assessments.mitigation: Review shooting logic interactions with input flags from engineer’s mechanic; add integration tests with auto-fire disabled scenarios and upgrade cap edge cases.
assessments.risk: Complex AI behaviour could delay or alter game tick performance; potential conflicts in shooting logic if auto-fire disable from engineer is active; upgrade selection logic needs rigorous capping validation.

assessments.mitigation: Coordinate player state management with researcher mechanic, ensuring independent autonomous firing unaffected by auto-fire disable; unify rendering layers for new effects to avoid clutter and confusion.
assessments.risk: Disabling player auto-fire may conflict with pet companion’s autonomous firing; shared player state flags could cause timing bugs; rendering multiple translucent effects risks UI clutter.

proposed_action.rationale: While all three proposals modify overlapping core symbols (tick, renderWorld), their features operate on logically distinct entities and effects—environmental hazard, AI pet, and unique enemy—making combined integration feasible with proper synchronization. Their separated concerns (gas cloud damage, pet shooting, auto-fire disable) minimize functional code collisions if state management and rendering priorities are carefully managed. The absence of existing conflicts in upgrade and spawn logic supports compatibility, provided integration testing and conflict mitigation steps are implemented as recommended.

producer.claim: Integrating the Designer's Periodic Toxic Gas Clouds, Researcher's Pet Companion Upgrade, and Engineer's Ghost Phaser Enemy features into Cataclysm 0.7 is feasible and creates substantial new playable content.
producer.rationale: All three features target distinct gameplay aspects: environmental hazard, AI ally, and enemy mechanics respectively, minimizing direct code conflicts despite overlapping core symbols like tick and renderWorld. The Critic confirmed their compatibility given proper synchronization of player state flags and rendering layers. Each feature adds new strategic layers: gas clouds enforce movement and map awareness; pet companion offers tactical fire support; ghost phaser enforces timing and avoidant play by disabling auto-fire. Mitigations address UI clutter, performance optimization, upgrade cap enforcement, and shot logic interlocks ensuring smooth coexistence.
objections: The hostile auto-fire disable mechanic may conflict with pet companion autonomous firing if not carefully managed.
Toxic gas clouds expanding in late-night play could pose performance risks on low-end mobile devices and visually clutter the screen with multiple translucent effects.
Complex state management is needed to prevent stacking or timing bugs in damage-over-time, auto-fire disable durations, and pet AI shooting cadence.

proposed_action.decision_reason: All three candidates provide unique, non-overlapping content that together enrich late-game strategic depth with environmental hazards, new AI companion ally, and novel enemy challenge. Their shared core updates require merged but manageable coordination of player state and rendering, achievable with structured interface contracts and integration plan.

integration_steps: Merge Designer.tick insertions to spawn and update toxic gas clouds without interfering with Researcher and Engineer tick logic by segmenting hazard updates first
Modify Researcher.tick to check player.autoFireDisabled before allowing pet companion to shoot, ensuring autonomous fire is unaffected by player disable
Engineer.tick manages ghost enemy behavior and toggles player.autoFireDisabled flag with cooldown; pet companion shooting reads this flag accordingly

RenderWorld modifications layered: first draw toxic gas clouds with subtle pulsing, then pet companion with distinct pet visual and shooting animations, finally ghost enemies with translucent ghost effect and UI auto-fire disable indicator
Update offerUpgrade and chooseUpgrade in Researcher to handle pet companion presence and lifecycle within upgrade cap constraints
Modify safeSpawn (Designer) to avoid spawning gas clouds near new pet companion spawn mechanics and ghost enemies
Add logging and stress tests verifying timing interactions between damage ticks, auto-fire disable durations, and pet shooting cadence
Implement combined performance optimizations as per Critic recommendations to maintain smooth HUD and input responsiveness
verification: Play from night 6 through 10 verifying ghost enemies spawn and player auto-fire disables at intervals with correct visual and functional feedback
At milestone level 3, confirm pet companion upgrade appears, can be selected, companion spawns and autonomously shoots at enemies dealing reduced damage
During night 8+, observe toxic gas clouds spawn at correct intervals, expand/shrink visually, deal damage when player is inside, and play notify messages and warning sounds
Verify pet companion autonomous shooting continues correctly when player's auto-fire is disabled, and stops when the companion timer expires

Validate no performance degradation or input lag on mobile emulation at 360x780 and 390x844 resolutions

Playtest session reports confirming player experience improvements and no UI clutter complaints

coder_report:
# Cataclysm 0.7 implementation

Implemented the agreed update in `docs/preview/game.js` and `docs/preview/index.html`. Selected candidate IDs: **designer**, **researcher**, **engineer**. Read job.json, plan.json (including update_decision.selection), feedback.md (empty array), and the existing runtime, markup, configuration and styles before editing. No private recording material was accessed or inferred. This is an implementation for runner acceptance, not a published or QA-approved release.

## Selected playable features

- **designer — Periodic Toxic Gas Clouds:** Added `hazards.toxicGasClouds`, spawn/exposure timers, `gasSpawn`, `gasRadius`, and `updateGas`. Starting night 8, a cloud appears every 30 simulation seconds, with a one-second green ring/text warning and synthesized warning tone before a six-second expansion/hold/shrink lifecycle. Spawn sites use existing safeSpawn with a 130px boundary margin, at least 250px from the player, and clearance from the pet and ghosts. Failed safe placement retries after one second. Staying in gas costs one HP per second; overlapping exposure uses one damage clock and respects existing invulnerability. Leaving resets exposure. Transparent circles render above city geometry, before the pet and enemies. Pulsing is omitted for reduced motion.
- **researcher — Pet Companion Upgrade:** Added the special upgrade button and availability/selection handling, `entities.petCompanion`, `summonPet`, and `updatePet`. Offered at level 3 and later third-level milestones, counted toward the existing four-special-pick budget. One pick before level 9; two total from level 9, with another summon unavailable while the first is active. Each selection summons a small gold cat for 35 simulation seconds. It independently follows the player and targets the nearest enemy within 420px, shooting every 0.8 seconds for half the player's current single-projectile damage (including rage). It has no spread or bounce bonuses. A muzzle ring and remaining-life label communicate activity. Projectiles use the existing collision, kill, fish and score pipeline.
- **engineer — Ghost Phaser Enemy:** Every ninth regular spawn from night 6 becomes a translucent violet ghost. It pursues directly through decorative city geometry, like the existing movement model, with distinct outline and color. Within 220px it seals player auto-fire for exactly two simulation seconds. A shared eight-second cooldown prevents multiple ghosts stacking or extending that seal. Added `updateGhosts`, player silence/cooldown state, a `shotAtEnemy` guard, notification, tone, and a FIRE SEALED ring/text indicator. Existing projectiles remain active.

## Shared contracts and reconciliation

- Adapted the proposal's `gameState` name to the existing closure-local `game`; no parallel state store was introduced. `game.player.autoFireDisabled` is a real boolean. `game.entities.petCompanion` and `game.hazards.toxicGasClouds` hold actual entities. Pet targeting/shooting lives in the segmented `updatePet` helper rather than object methods, matching the runtime's existing procedural style.
- The plan contradicts itself: one contract says the disable flag controls both guns, while Critic guidance and explicit verification require autonomous pet shooting to continue during silence. Implemented the explicit gameplay verification: the flag gates only player fire; pet fire uses its independent timer. This is an intentional reconciliation, not an omitted selected feature.
- `tick` updates gas first, then ghost silence, then pet AI before player movement/fire and existing enemy/projectile resolution. Each helper runs only during a running simulation. Upgrades and pause freeze all new timers. Restart recreates all new state.
- Rendering orders gas before pet before enemies, with ghosts last within the enemy group; the player and its status feedback remain visible above them. Bounded cloud lifetime/cadence, one nearest-enemy scan only when pet shooting is due, existing enemy/projectile budgets, and simple Canvas primitives limit added work.
- The existing special-upgrade counters plus `petPicks` enforce the shared budget; existing upgrade menu code disables unavailable choices. Existing scrolling menu accommodates the added option.
- Preserved canvas and all control IDs, touch release/cancellation and Samsung fallback, keyboard movement, pause/resume/restart, score formula, boss flow, storage keys, sound controls, configuration fetch with no-store, and diagnostic interface. Extended read-only snapshots with copied pet/gas state, silence/cooldown/pet-pick fields and projectile damage for observability. No writable diagnostic controls were added.
- Set code/boot/display version to 0.7 and HTML run/cache identifiers to 42312781802-1. Preserved `game-version` and existing boot handshake. Added field-guide explanations. Build metadata and publishing code were not modified.

## Checks actually run

- `node --check docs/preview/game.js` — passed, including final run.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `node game_factory/mobile_acceptance.cjs` — attempted; failed before any page loaded. Chromium exited with SIGTRAP after `crashpad/util/linux/socket.cc:45 setsockopt: Operation not permitted`. No touch/mobile acceptance pass is claimed, and the supplied test was not modified.
- `node /tmp/cat-content-test.cjs` — passed after correcting an incomplete mock DOM parentElement in the temporary harness. Harness loaded the actual game source in Node VM, exposing closure functions only in memory; shipped code has no test-state mutation interface. Assertions covered level-3 pet availability/selection, active-pet disabling, level-9 second-tier and four-pick caps, half-damage pet shots during player silence, player firing suppression, two-second expiry without stacking, pet lifetime expiry, night-6 ghost spawn gate, pre-night-8 gas absence, safe cloud position, radius lifecycle, exposure damage, cloud removal, pause freeze, and clean restart.
- The same temporary harness executed the actual renderWorld with a mock Canvas while all three mechanics were present, then 1,800 actual simulation ticks with high test-only HP and combined content. Final measured loop time: 13.8ms on this Node host; enemy/cloud bounds passed. This excludes browser rendering, audio, device performance and real input, so it is not a mobile frame-rate benchmark.

## Remaining verification limits

Browser launch restrictions prevented local 360x780/390x844 touch checks, visual inspection and browser-error checks. Audio was code-path checked with mocked browser facilities, not auditioned. Natural full-session progression through nights 6–10, physical-phone performance, player-experience/UI-clutter feedback, and production hash/live-byte delivery remain unverified. No playtest opinions, independent QA approval, accepted receipt, deployment, or production release is claimed. The runner must complete those acceptance/delivery stages.
